title: Weekly release orchestra: RC governance, LTS demarcation, and automated notes playbook
creator: Priya Desai
description: Define and implement a resilient weekly release orchestration playbook that standardizes RC tagging, LTS lane demarcation, rollout gates, and fully automates release notes generation. Goal: make weekly candidate creation deterministic, surface gating signals earlier, and enable safe automated promotion to stable/LTS lanes with clear rollback paths.
acceptance_criteria: CI job 'weekly-candidate-orchestrator' creates RC tags with deterministic names according to naming convention
Release notes are generated automatically from merged PR metadata and curated changelog entries and published to the release page within 10 minutes of tag creation
Canary/Canary-A/B gating rules execute on the RC and provide pass/fail signal visible in Console runbook
Automated fallback lane triggers a warm standby model variant (lower-cost) when SLO breach detected during promotion window
LTS lane demarcation enforced by branch-protection and automated validation; cannot be promoted without LTS-approval label and passing regressions suite

steps: Define RC naming scheme: release-YYYY.MM.WW-rcN (automatically incremented per week)
Add a deterministic CI job that runs at weekly cut window and builds candidate artifacts and tags the repo
Collect gating signals: unit/integration test pass, e2e smoke, perf smoke (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec), storage/IO health, and model quality regression checks
Implement release-notes-generator: aggregate PR titles, authors, changelog fragments, and opt-in highlight blocks; persist artifact to S3 and publish URL to release page
Wire Console cards for RC health and next promotion ETA, including runbook links and contact on-call
Create promotion job with staged rollouts: canary -> broad canary -> staged -> stable; each stage requires defined SLO thresholds and vote windows
Add automated fallback: on SLO breach during promotion, demote and route to fallback variant and notify stakeholders
Enforce LTS promotion guard rails: require 'lts-approve' label, passing nightly LTS regression suite, and architecture lead approval
Document rollback steps and automate emergency rollback playbook in GitHub Actions and Console Runbook
decisions: Adopt hybrid semantic/time-based versioning: weekly candidate names are time-based; stable releases map to semver (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) with LTS lane carrying MAJOR.MINOR-LTS tags
RCs will be auto-generated weekly but promotions to stable are gated and require either automated pass or explicit approval for LTS
Release notes will be primarily automated but allow curated human highlight sections using a '/release-note' PR label
Promotion windows will be 90 minutes by default with configurable extension in case of transient infra noise
risks: Automation bugs could create incorrectly named tags or overwrite RC metadata; mitigation: strong integration tests and dry-run mode
Over-automation may prematurely promote regressions if gating signals are miscalibrated; mitigation: staged rollout and human approval for LTS
Timing mismatch across regions could cause inconsistent behaviour on Dedicated/Private installs; mitigation: region-aware promotion scheduling
Release notes automation may omit critical context; mitigation: mandatory human review for security/compat changes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): implement deterministic tagger CI job and notes generator in dry-run mode; Phase 2 (week 3-4): enable gating metrics and Console health card; Phase 3 (week 5): turn on automatic promotions for non-LTS stable with canary stage only; Phase 4 (week 6+): enable LTS guards and rollback automation. Monitor via release-orchestra dashboard and iterate weekly.
